question.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
{[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have been given the following diagonalization of $A:$

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Since $A=PD{P}^{-1}$, we can compute ${A}^{k}$ by using the formula 

$$
{A}^{k}=P{D}^{k}{P}^{-1}.
$$

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{71} & =P{D}^{71}{P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{71}(\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}(-1)^{71} & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{71}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
